text.p: H.F. Ahmanson & Co., currently in a takeover battle for rival California savings and loan Great Western Financial Corp., reported higher-than-expected earnings Tuesday.
The Irwindale, Calif.-based parent company of Home Savings of America, reported that net income rose 59 percent in the first quarter to $103.1 million, or 87 cents per share.
The figure was far ahead of the 70 cents per share estimated by analysts. In the last quarter of 1996 net income was $64.7 million, or 45 cents per share.
Results for 1997 included an after-tax gain on the sale of the company's Arizona branch system of $9.5 million, or 8 cents per share.
Net interest income totalled $317.6 million for the first quarter of 1997 vs. $317.0 million a year earlier.
In the first quarter of 1997, noninterest income, excluding the gain on the sale of the Arizona branches, was $72.9 million, up from $60.5 million reported in the year-ago quarter.
Ahmanson has $48.7 billion in assets and operates 380 financial service centres in three states and 124 mortgage lending offices in eight states.

Ahmanson initially launched a hostile bid in mid-February for Great Western and has been tenaciously fighting to complete the deal despite Great Western's rejection and its merger agreement, announced March 6, with white knight Washington Mutual Inc., which is based in Seattle.
